newsitem.title: UK: Witness in Grobbelaar case charged.
newsitem.headline: Witness in Grobbelaar case charged.

text.p: The chief prosection witness in the trial of goalkeeper Bruce Grobbelaar and two other stars of British soccer accused of rigging matches was charged on Thursday with attempting to pervert the course of justice.
Police said Chris Vincent, a Zimbabwean businessman, was charged after he was questioned at Aldershot police station in southern England. Vincent, 37, was arrested by police on Tuesday.
"He will be appearing in court on Friday," a police spokesman said.

Grobbelaar, who played for Southampton and Liverpool and is now with Plymouth, retired Aston Villa striker John Fashanu and Dutch-born Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Seger are accused of giving and taking bribes to fix the result of matches.
They were charged after a police investigation prompted by media claims about the activities of an Asian gambling syndicate in England's premier league.
Among the charges, Grobbelaar is accused of accepting 2,000 pounds ($3,131) from Vincent, his former business partner, in November 1994 for throwing an unspecified match. ($1=.6388 Pound)
